title: Initial division invariant
statement: For every bit string $z$, the initial state formed by pairing the second projection of $z$ with the pairing of the reverse of its first projection and two empty strings satisfies the following invariant: there exist bit strings $R,r,q$ such that the state is the nested pairing of the second projection of $z$, $R$, and the pair $(r,q)$; $|r|+|R|$ and $|q|+|R|$ are each at most the length of the first projection of $z$; and, if the value of the second projection is positive, then $(\operatorname{val}(q)\operatorname{val}(\pi_2 z)+\operatorname{val}(r))2^{|R|}+\operatorname{val}(R^{\mathrm{rev}})=\operatorname{val}(\pi_1 z)$ and $\operatorname{val}(r)<\operatorname{val}(\pi_2 z)$. Here bit strings are valued in little-endian binary, and $\pi_1,\pi_2$ denote the total first and second projections of the self-delimiting pair encoding, with empty string returned when decoding fails.
hypotheses_covered: The positivity condition on the second projection, as the antecedent of the invariant's conditional clause
